recipes.name: Butternut Mascarpone Gnocchi
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
0.25 cup thinly sliced fresh sage leaves

steps.text: Trim stem and cut butternut squash in half lengthwise. Place in a microwave-safe dish, cover with plastic wrap, and microwave until tender, about 8 minutes. Transfer to paper towels to cool. Discard skin and set squash aside.
Whisk mascarpone cheese, 1/2 cup Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, eggs, salt, and black pepper in a bowl until smooth. Whisk in butternut squash until blended.
Whisk in 1/2 cup flour until just incorporated. Whisk in remaining 1/2 cup flour, stirring until flour just disappears. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Melt about 1/3 of the butter in large nonstick skillet; remove from heat.

Scoop out approximately 1 1/2 teaspoons of the butternut squash dough with a spoon. Using a second spoon, push the dough off the first spoon and into the boiling water. Repeat with remaining dough, working in batches of 12 to 15 gnocchi at a time. When a gnocchi rise to the surface, cook for 1 additional minute, then transfer with a slotted spoon to the melted butter in the skillet.

Place the skillet over medium-high heat; cook gnocchi until golden brown on one side, about 3 minutes. Season with cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Turn gnocchi over and stir in sage leaves. Cook until second side is golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer to plate and drizzle with browned butter from the skillet. Garnish with 1 tablespoon Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Butternut Mascarpone Gnocchi
raw_recipe.description: Incredibly light and delicious, these gnocchi feature butternut squash and mascarpone cheese with a hint of sage.

review.reviewBody: I changed it a bit. I substituted cream cheese & sour cream (6 ounces and 2 ounces) for the marscapone and used a kabocha squash instead of butternut. I also chopped up some portabello mushrooms and sauteed them in the butter and served over top. Outstanding!

It’s a crowd pleaser. I used a small scoop instead of 2 spoons. Smoother gnocchi don’t fall apart as much in the water. I also brought the water down to a simmer instead of a rolling boil. I cooked the gnocchi in batches through the simmering and sautéing steps then started the next batch. I prefer fresh basil instead of fresh sage.

I had to exercise my noodle a bit with this recipe because it didn't spell out every step. That's okay. Here's what I learned after reading the comments and going through the process. Weigh the squash. Don't rush the refrigeration time, however tempting. Use a gentle boil. A rolling boil is too strong. Test for doneness by lifting the dumplings with a spider and poking them. If they're on the mushy side, let them cook. They're ready when they're firm. Set them aside on a plate until it's time for the next stage. Fry them in a non-stick pan in stages, refreshing the butter and sage each time. Store the finished ones on a plate in a warm oven. Serve. Wonderful!

I followed the recipe exactly but they came out mushy. Perhaps my squash had too much excess water in it? I didn't want to waste the batter so transformed it into pancake batter. I added two tsp baking powder and 1 tsp baking soda, a bit of milk and a little more flour to get it to the right pancake batter consistency. They were great as pancakes and the maple syrup went nice with the light cheese flavouring.

These are amazing! I forgot to take a picture because I couldn't wait to eat them. Used Kabocha squash that had been roasted days earlier and was looking for a way to finish it off. Did not have Mascarpone so I used half sour cream and half finely grated Swiss cheese. I also used whole wheat flour because I didn't have white flour. They were still light and fluffy. This recipe is a keeper. Also, watching the video was helpful.
We loved it! I halved this recipe and I had plenty. I used a mixture of cream cheese and goat cheese and I roasted the squash in my oven. I will definitely make this again.

This was amazing! Seriously, I can't rave enough about it. Used precut butternut squash to save time. Also, didn't bother refrigerating it due to time constraints and it turned out great. Will be making this again and again!!

I don't live near a grocery store so had to substitute 1/2 cup cream cheese and 1/2 cup sour cream for the mascarpone. It was a big hit with my foodie friends. I can't wait to try it with the mascarpone. If you failed with gnocchi before, don't let it stop you from trying this!
Had a hard time getting these to hold together. Ended up adding a lot more flour and boiling for longer.

These gnocchi are so delectable eaten right out of the pan while they're hot. But unfortunately it makes a mess and they cool off quickly so I put them in a 200 oven to keep them warm. Also, you have to make them the day before. Lots of time put into this. Otherwise, I'd give them a 5.

The recipe sounded great and the flavors too. Unfortunately the dough was far too gooey and runny. I attempted to save it but adding more flour too away from the other flavors like the parm and squash. Next time I’ll ensure the squash is drained better and dec the wet ingredients.

I made this recipe exactly as the chefs video. Absolutely heaven on a fork. When you add the sage leaves you are infusing the butter with sage, I like my sage crispy such a delicious addition to the dish. My company rated this a 5/5.

I made this for a party and the flavors for the few Gnocchi that made it was GREAT but the final presentation for these was flimsy . Chef John recipes i find are always great and his clear witty instructions are very helpful . I followed the recipe exactly , but like other reviewers, I found that the Gnocchi tended to fall apart ( even after setting the mixture overnight and cooling them after boil for a few hours for a party prier to frying) . i haven't given up on finding an alternative way to keep the wonderful taste of these but an alternative method for texture

These were a total disaster, I wasted so much time roasting a squash and refrigerating the batter for twelve hours. I knew right away they weren’t going to work when they started falling apart in the water.

I could not wait to make it after watching the video, and I was not disappointed. It was so delicious. I made it in NEWFOUNDLAND FOR MY SON’S family, I made it in Nova Scotia to share with friends, and I am making in tonight and tomorrow in Calgary for my family here. I brought some when I came to Calgary. They loved it. Worth the time.

I made it not once.. Twice. this recipe is fooling. I followed it to the exact letter and both times it let me down. I wasted a lot of money, time and gardening due to this recipe. I am sure that it will work for some people, but be warned, there are pitfalls that will leave you with no meal at all. Here is what I experienced: 1st attempt; made as shown, and overcooked the items during boiling stage and it dissolved in the pot. I realized I did not let the "batter" set 8 hours or overnight.. so night 2.. cold batter, set for 12 hours. attempted again, this time, making sure to pull the gnocchi off the boiling water at the 1 min. marker. I had butter prewarmed and ready to fry in a pan next to it. Even after being parboiled, the gnocchi,fell apart and crumbled during the last stage. I feel there are several caveat's left out of this recipe and it is made to seem much easier than it is. I will never attempt this mess of a meal again.
I baked the squash to impart more flavor, but they were still very bland. Did not like the texture. Too mushy.

Having never made Gnocchi before I didn't know what to expect. These little buggers were delicious! It was quite a lot of busy work but so good! I made my little balls ahead of time and placed them in the boiling water about 15 at a time. They did stick to the wax paper but it made the process go a little faster.

I agree with another reviewer that it mostly tasted like butter, and we had to fry them longer (until almost burnt) to make the texture so they weren’t falling apart or mashing each other when placed in a bowl. To be fair, made it with ricotta instead of marscapone cheese, so don’t know if that would make any difference. A lot of work for a side dish...
I followed the directions exactly but it came out a wet sticky mess instead of a dough. I tried adding more flour but by the time it finally felt like dough it was too much flour..
